claim: For humans, the same formal puzzle (Tower of Hanoi isomorph) is much harder when its rules must be held in memory than when the display enforces them. External rules produced no rule errors. For LLMs the isolated test is still missing: external sound checkers beat self-checking by 30 to 50 points for GPT-4 (d12) and environment rule-violation messages help every frontier VLM (d14), but rules-in-prompt vs rules-in-checker on one puzzle was not found. A 2022 human study qualifies it: the display raised completion but cost more moves (d18).
agent_test: Same task twice at equal tokens: rules restated in prose vs rules enforced by a checker that rejects illegal steps. Count rule-violation rate and solve rate.

claim: Externalising constraints does two things at once: it lowers memory load and it steers which strategy is found (recursive smallest-first move). The two are not separated in the founding paper.
agent_test: Compare (a) a checker that only rejects illegal steps with (b) a checker that also lists legal moves. If (b) beats (a), the strategy cue matters beyond load.

claim: Using position (location) to carry a dimension beat size or colour coding for the same structure in humans; step counts rarely reached significance.
agent_test: Encode a state as a position-keyed table vs a labelled list; same facts, equal tokens; measure accuracy.

claim: An external copy helps working memory only if its format matches how the internal copy was encoded. A mismatched mix of memory plus display can be worse than all-internal (Exp 2 length 3 errors: E-E 1.1%, E-I 15.9%, I-I 20.5%; Exp 1 length 3: E-I 8.9% vs I-I 4.2%).
agent_test: Give the agent notes in the order it will use them vs a mismatched order; compare error rate.

claim: Diagrams help human deduction only when they make the alternative cases explicit; a decorative diagram had no effect.
agent_test: Case-split table vs plain premises on disjunctive logic items, plus a decorative variant as control.

claim: For LLMs, the way the same data is serialised changes accuracy, sometimes by tens of points, and the best format differs by model and task. Newer data: std over four syntax encodings 3.5 to 10.5 points (gpt-oss smallest, fine-tuned graph models largest; d09); the same SPaRC puzzle moves from 14.4 (image) to 38.0 (text) to 48.4 (image with symbols) on Qwen 3.5 397B (d06).
agent_test: Run each scaffold comparison over 3 or more formats of the same state and report the range, not one run.

claim: Graph encodings that keep the facts a query needs adjacent (incident list) beat scattered ones (adjacency list): 19.8% vs 53.8% on connected nodes, PaLM 62B zero-shot. No single encoding wins across tasks. 2025-26 data: adjacency list beat edge list on 3B models for graph metrics, while sorted edge lists stay near default for larger models and matrices lose (d09, d10). No incident-vs-adjacency test on a frontier model was found.
agent_test: Store linked state per entity (incident style) vs as an edge list; test relation queries.

claim: Table format effects are real but usually a few points (HTML vs markdown etc., GPT-3.5/4). Putting the question before the data (+6.81 points lost when after) and showing a format example help.
agent_test: Place the question before vs after the state block at equal tokens.

claim: Having a model draw its own state as a text grid after each step (VoT) beats CoT on spatial tasks (NL navigation 59.0 vs 54.0 CoT vs 35.5 no-viz, GPT-4; tiling 63.9 vs 54.2 vs 47.0), but the gain over CoT on NL navigation is not significant (p<0.16) and only one group reported it.
agent_test: Add per-step grid redraw to a spatial item set; compare with CoT at equal tokens.

claim: Model-drawn states are often wrong (state accuracy about 24-26%) and correct decisions follow in 65-77% only when the drawing was right. The representation needs its own check. 2026 Text2Space: layouts built from text were right 28 to 51% of the time (five of six models) and writing them first never raised answer accuracy; answers where layout and answer agree were right 88 to 97% vs 71 to 94% overall, but 24 to 54% of items disagreed (d08). A check is therefore a filter with a coverage cost; token cost was not measured.
agent_test: Verify each redrawn state by code against ground truth; correlate state accuracy with final correctness.

claim: Drawing and visual scaffolds do not help uniformly. They lose to text when the structure is easy in text (VoT ring task 49.5 vs 52.5 CoT; WoT square grid 50 vs 98 CoT; MVoT text coordinates over 95% on simple grids). They win when geometry or entity count is awkward (WoT hexagon 8 to 61; FrozenLake text CoT below Direct). Rule supported by 2024-26 data: text or ASCII wins for small symbolic grids and entity lists (SpatialEval; VisGym GPT-5 3 to 4 times better in ASCII; o4-mini best text-only); a layout or image wins when positional relations scale with size (transpose text 92.7% to 0.8%, image 90.8% at 20x20, fine-tuned models) or glyph shape matters (Matchstick). It is model-specific: Gemini 2.5 Pro gained from vision on easy Wood Slide, o4-mini did not.
agent_test: Route per item: text state for simple layouts, drawn or tabular state for awkward ones; compare with always-draw and never-draw.

claim: A self-generated rendered state diagram inside search lifts planning sharply (Blocksworld simple 35.5 to 90.2 for GPT-4o; text-only optimized GoT 58; Claude 3.5 Sonnet 54.8 to 98). Handing the model the plotting code instead of the image dropped it to 24, below baseline. Authors' own text and table disagree in places.
agent_test: Compact rendered state vs generator code vs prose in a planning loop at equal tokens.

claim: Giving a multimodal model drawing tools raises math and vision scores (average +12.7 math, +8.6 vision; GPT-4o max-flow +41.3), but the gain depends on the reader parsing the sketch (relative depth +12.1 GPT-4o vs +2.4 GPT-4 Turbo). On current frontier models the tool gain is model-specific: GPT-5 lost 11 to 14 points without image tools, Gemini 2.5 Pro gained 2.7 without them (d21); a constraint-checked canvas added 0 (Gemini 3 Flash), 3 (Sonnet 4.6) and 6 (GPT-5.4) correct items of 112 on OlympiadBench (d11).
agent_test: Sketch tool on vs off; check legibility with a second reading.

claim: Rendered diagrams did not reliably help two LLMs on syllogisms (Euler and linear diagrams equal or lower than text). The conversion-case drop is only 2 to 3 items out of 19 (Sonnet NL 16/19, Linear 13/19, Euler 14/19) and is not significant on my unpaired test (p 0.45 to 0.69), so it should not be quoted as a diagram-format effect. Labels are balanced (95 each) and all conversion items are neutral; GPT-4o-mini's weak neutral score (24/95) is answer bias. Earlier work by the same group reported some Euler gains; human studies report diagram gains (d19).
agent_test: Run the same notations on our own logic items; use a countermodel search, not a picture.

claim: Vision-language models misread simple diagrams and prefer text over the picture when they conflict, so image diagrams are an unreliable channel for fine detail.
agent_test: Prefer structured text state; if images are used, add a text-vs-image consistency check.

claim: Linear free-text traces are weak for global graph structure; special topologies and harder tasks defeat standard prompting.
agent_test: Explicit structured scratch graph vs prose reasoning on connectivity items.

claim: Output notation can decide measured success: asking for a generating function instead of a 32,767-move list at N=15 can avoid output-length failure. Support is one unreviewed arXiv comment with no counts and an admitted low-power sample (d01). An independent replication with stepwise prompting still saw collapse near 8 disks (10 trials per N, d02), and a second comment is anecdotal and argues tool use is the fix (d03). 'Answer notation matters' is plausible; 'collapse is only a format artefact' is not shown.
agent_test: Request a program vs an exhaustive list on the same long-horizon task at equal output budget.

claim: Forcing reasoning into a table (Tab-CoT) gives a small average gain over free-text zero-shot CoT (+2.2 average, 5 of 6 arithmetic tasks).
agent_test: Tabular step log vs prose steps, equal tokens.

claim: Writing intermediate steps (scratchpad, CoT) is the base external representation for a model; the benefit depends on scale and on training or prompting.
agent_test: Use this as the baseline arm in every notation comparison.

claim: Surface form of the same logical problem changes LLM answers (content effects, counterfactual formats, layout changes), so a scaffold tuned on one notation may not transfer. 2026 data: five current models on 85 isomorphic algebra problems flipped correctness across forms, with small effect sizes (Cramers V 0.03 to 0.07 between interfaces; d13).
agent_test: Isomorphic rewrites of each test item; report the spread.

claim: A second representation costs translation effort: perceived load rose first when students learned problem-appropriate diagrams and fell only later; multiple representations can hurt. LLM proxy only: when a model writes both an ASCII layout and an answer, the two disagree on 24 to 54 percent of items (d08); no study measured extra tokens for keeping two state formats.
agent_test: Count extra tokens spent translating between two state formats vs accuracy gained.

claim: Larkin and Simon's core claim (location indexing cuts search and recognition) is the theory base. Its full text was blocked by the publisher and has not been opened in either session; support remains recall plus citation in Zhang and Wang (d22 is the same lab as Zhang and Norman). No replication or failed replication of Larkin and Simon or of Zhang and Norman was found in 800 to 1,000 scanned citing titles each (d23).
agent_test: Not directly testable; see K03 and K07 for operational tests.

claim: No LLM study of true representational isomorphs of one puzzle (Hanoi cups vs pegs) was found. The nearest tests keep items fixed and change the notation: ARC object encoding 13/50 to 23/50 for GPT-4 (d04), SPaRC image 14.4 / text 38.0 / image with symbols 48.4 (d06), and 85 algebra problems in four forms across five models with small effects (d13). The direct analogue of Zhang and Norman is still untested.
agent_test: Run one puzzle in 3 isomorphic surface forms at equal tokens; measure solve rate.

claim: Replacing a flat text grid with an object-level encoding built by an external tool raises GPT-4 on ARC-like tasks from 13/50 to 23/50 (full ARC training set 81/400 to 97/400) and removes the horizontal vs vertical gap. Same items, only the notation changed.
agent_test: Give the agent an object list (id, colour, cells, bounding box) beside the raw grid on ARC items; compare with the grid alone at equal tokens.

claim: A checker that returns explicit rule-violation messages helps frontier models: removing text feedback about illegal moves lowered every model in VisGym, and sound external critique lifted GPT-4 by 30 to 50 points over self-critique. The human result of zero rule errors with display-enforced rules has not been reproduced for an LLM with rules-in-prompt as the control.
agent_test: Run the same puzzle with rules only in the prompt vs a legality checker that rejects moves; report illegal-move rate and solve rate.

claim: On current frontier and reasoning models the evidence that drawing or a visual channel helps is mixed and model-specific: o4-mini was best with text only while Gemini 2.5 Pro used vision for fewer tokens; GPT-5 gained 11 to 14 points from image tools while Gemini 2.5 Pro gained nothing; a constraint-checked canvas gave 0 to 6 of 112 items; Visual Thinking beat o1-preview on hard but not on simple planning. No study re-ran VoT or WoT with a 2025-26 reasoning model as the base.
agent_test: Run the agent's own model with the visual or drawn state on and off; do not import gains measured on other models.

claim: Layout beats flat text when positional relations scale with size: fine-tuned models on transpose, Game of Life and LU fell with text (92.7% to 0.8%; 86.5% to 46.6%) while the rendered layout stayed above 90 to 99 percent within the trained range. For small grids and text-describable entities, text equals or beats the picture. The cross-over evidence comes from small fine-tuned models and synthetic tasks.
agent_test: Sweep grid size on one task in text vs layout; find the size where the order flips for the agent's model.

claim: Asking the model to draw its state before answering did not raise answer accuracy in any of six models (Text2Space), because the drawn layout was right only 28 to 51% of the time (five of six models; Qwen2.5-7B 12.5%); a code check of layout against answer works as a filter (kept answers 88 to 97% correct for the four larger models) at a cost of dropping 24 to 54% of items.
agent_test: Write the state, check it by code, answer only from checked states; report accuracy on kept items, share dropped, and tokens per kept item.

claim: For graph facts a sorted edge list is stable for current larger models (std across four syntaxes 3.5 to 5.4 points for gpt-oss) while fine-tuned graph models vary 9.7 to 10.5; adjacency matrices often lose; adjacency lists shift counting tasks; small 3B models favour adjacency lists for metrics. No frontier head-to-head of incident list, adjacency list, edge list and table exists.
agent_test: Test a sorted edge list vs an adjacency list vs a per-entity incident list on the agent's own relational state.
